what_it_does: This paper accelerates point-cloud neural networks (PointNets)—AI models that process 3D point clouds from LiDAR sensors in autonomous vehicles and robotics. These networks have a critical bottleneck: farthest-point sampling, a step that iteratively finds the most distant point from existing points—which becomes quadratically slow as the cloud grows. Nebula replaces this slow serial search with fast block-based partitioning, then exploits a key insight: many intermediate calculations are wasted because they operate on points that will be discarded anyway. By skipping these redundant operations and rearranging memory accesses to be more regular, Nebula reduces latency and power consumption per operation.
